scheduler.wait.block_unavailable: Holding until the job ends is only available in the terminal; here the job runs in the background.
scheduler.wait.background_hint: It runs in the background and this terminal says when it ends. Check: /jobs show %s. Stop: /jobs cancel %s. Add --block to hold the prompt instead.
scheduler.wait.background_hint_quiet: It runs in the background. Check: /jobs show %s. Stop: /jobs cancel %s.
scheduler.wait.usage_background: The wait runs in the background and the terminal says when it ends. --block holds the prompt (Ctrl+C lets go; the job keeps running). --quiet skips the notice.
scheduler.follow.started: Holding the prompt until job %s ends. Ctrl+C lets go of it; the job keeps running.
scheduler.follow.lost: Lost track of job %s: it was removed from history or the scheduler stopped answering.
scheduler.follow.detached: Prompt released. Job %s keeps running in the background: /jobs show %s.
scheduler.notify.timed_out: Wait %s (%s) timed out after %s; the condition was never met.
scheduler.jobs.ambiguous: %s matches more than one job. Use the full ID from /jobs list --all.
scheduler.jobs.clear.none: No finished jobs match the filter; nothing to clear.
scheduler.jobs.clear.rerun: Run the same command again with --yes (or -y) to delete them.
sched.jobs.sub.wait: Hold the prompt until a job ends
sched.flag.block: Hold the prompt until the wait ends (default: background)
sched.flag.quiet: Do not announce the end of the job in the terminal
sched.flag.notify: Announce the end of the job (or of each cycle) in the terminal
sched.jobs.wait.flag.timeout: Stop holding the prompt after this long (the job keeps running)
